land.text: Louis II's share of the 1255 partition, 'the Palatinate and Upper Bavaria' (Louis the Strict page)

predecessors.note: The stem duchy is much older (Duchy of Bavaria page: 'First partition: 1255', capital 'Regensburg (until 1255)'); Cliopatria has no Bavaria row before 1260, so the map enters the duchy as Upper Bavaria after the 1255 partition. Lower Bavaria went to Henry XIII in 1255 and is, by its outline, Cliopatria's 'House of Wittelsbach' row (1260-1332); it rejoins this state in 1340.

land.text: 'The electorate existed until 1806, when Bavaria was proclaimed a kingdom' (Electorate of Bavaria page)

successors.note: Maximilian IV Joseph was proclaimed King Maximilian I Joseph on 1 January 1806, the day after this dossier's last year closes; the same ruler and state continue, so the colour agent may treat the two Cliopatria rows (Q47261 and Q154195) as one state.

capitals.name: Munich
capitals.note: 'The main residences of Louis were at Alter Hof located at the very north-eastern part of Munich and Heidelberg Castle' (Louis the Strict page); the Duchy of Bavaria infobox gives 'Regensburg (until 1255) Munich (from 1505)'. Landshut was the seat of the Bavaria-Landshut line 1353-1503 (infobox 'Capital: Landshut'); one dot is kept at Munich.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1260-1267 only: Louis II's Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate

keyframe_review.note: 28.7 k km2: Upper Bavaria with the Rhenish Palatinate. 'When the Wittelsbach country was divided in 1255 among Otto's sons, Louis received the Palatinate and Upper Bavaria, while his brother duke Henry XIII of Bavaria received Lower Bavaria'; the Duchy of Bavaria page adds 'a division of the land into Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate and the Nordgau (headquartered in Munich)'. Lower Bavaria is, by its outline (bbox 10.9-13.8 E), Cliopatria's House of Wittelsbach row. Neither page gives an infobox area. The outline stands; only the years change, because the 1268 inheritance (below) is dated by the page and Cliopatria enlarges the shape in 1272.

correction.text: the 1260 holdings plus 'some of Conradin's possessions' inherited in 1268, as Cliopatria draws them from 1272

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1268-1271: 'After the young prince's execution in Naples in 1268, Louis inherited some of Conradin's possessions in Swabia'. Cliopatria draws the larger outline (35.8 k km2, 7.0 k km2 more) only from 1272 and keeps a Hohenstaufen row to 1271, so the hand-over is four years late. The page names Swabia, but the cells the 1272 outline adds (gazetteer: about 8.6 k km2) lie between 7.8 and 12.6 E and north of 48.9 N, in the Palatinate and the Nordgau rather than in Swabia: the year is the page's, the place is not confirmed.

35.8 k km2 for 1272-1278: Upper Bavaria, the Palatinate and Conradin's inheritance of 1268 (see duchy-of-bavaria_1268 for the four-year lag). No infobox area on the pages opened; the added 7.0 k km2 are not located by any page.

35.3 k km2, 0.4 k km2 less than 1272-1278: an outline change that no page opened explains ('page silent'); no territorial event is claimed for 1279. 'supported the election of the Habsburg Rudolph I against Ottokar II in 1273' is political, not territorial.

35.3 k km2, unchanged in substance. 'Louis died at Heidelberg on 2 February 1294' and was 'succeeded by his eldest surviving son Rudolf I'; the Louis IV page has Louis IV 'Duke of Upper Bavaria from 1294 to 1301 together with his elder brother'. A joint reign, no change of land.

35.2 k km2 for 1305-1325. 'In 1310, there was a dispute between the brothers over the inheritance of their father' (Louis IV page) but no land change is dated. Cliopatria's row stops after 1325 and has nothing for 1326-1351; the new keyframes below carry the duchy through those years.

correction.text: Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate and the Nordgau, as in 1305-1325, until the Treaty of Pavia of 1329

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1326-1328: Cliopatria has no Duchy of Bavaria shape here; its Margraviate of Brandenburg row (77.8 k km2 in 1326-1332, bbox 7.0-16.9 E) lumps Brandenburg with the Wittelsbach lands of Bavaria. Louis IV was 'Duke of Upper Bavaria 1301-1347' (page), so the 1305 outline is carried to the Treaty of Pavia. The margraviate-of-brandenburg dossier should take Bavaria out of its 1326-1351 shapes.

correction.text: Upper Bavaria alone after the Palatinates left in 1329

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1329-1339: 'In the 1329 Treaty of Pavia, Emperor Louis divided ownership in a Palatine region, with the Rhine Palatinate, and a later so-called Upper Palatinate' (Duchy of Bavaria page); the Louis IV page says 'he gave the Palatinate to the two dukes'. Left is Upper Bavaria, drawn as the 1450 outline minus Cliopatria's Lower Bavaria (House of Wittelsbach). Lower Bavaria belongs to the Lower Bavarian dukes until 1340 and Cliopatria's Wittelsbach row ends in 1332, so 1333-1339 Lower Bavaria is nobody's in the data (see notes).

correction.text: Upper and Lower Bavaria reunited under Louis IV in 1340

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1340-1341: 'With the death of duke John I in 1340 Louis inherited Lower Bavaria and then reunited the duchy of Bavaria.' (The same page also says that at Pavia he 'inherited both Upper and Lower Bavaria for himself'; the dated sentence is the 1340 one.) Drawn as the Cliopatria 1450 outline, which is Upper plus Lower Bavaria (36.2 k km2).

correction.text: Bavaria reunited, with Tyrol in Wittelsbach hands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1342-1351: 'In 1342 Louis also acquired Tyrol for the Wittelsbach'; the County of Tyrol page: 'In 1342 she married Louis V of Wittelsbach, then Margrave of Brandenburg.' Tyrol is drawn as Cliopatria draws it in 1352 (the 1352 outline minus the 1363 one, about 16.8 k km2). Tyrol has no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet; a County of Tyrol dossier should take it over (see notes). Brandenburg is not drawn here: it is the margraviate-of-brandenburg state.

correction.text: Bavaria proper plus Tyrol; Brandenburg removed

keyframe_review.note: 97.2 k km2 is not Bavaria alone: Bavaria proper (the 1450 outline, 36.2 k km2) + Brandenburg (about 44 k km2: Cliopatria's Margraviate of Brandenburg shape of 1344-1351 is 80.5 k km2 and contains Bavaria's 36.2 k) + Tyrol (about 16.8 k km2) add up to 97 k. Brandenburg: 'In 1351, Louis gave the Mark to his younger half-brothers' Louis the Roman and Otto V; it is the margraviate-of-brandenburg state and is removed here, to be drawn there for 1352-1373. Tyrol stays (Wittelsbach until 1363). The pages give no infobox area.

correction.text: Bavaria proper (Upper and Lower Bavaria); Brandenburg and the Dutch counties removed

keyframe_review.note: 92.1 k km2 = Bavaria proper 36.2 k + Brandenburg about 44 k + Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut 11.6 k. Tyrol leaves in 1363: 'she bequeathed the county to Rudolph IV of Habsburg, Duke of Austria in 1363'. Brandenburg was sold in 1373 ('Charles succeeded in purchasing Brandenburg from Margrave Otto for 500,000 guilders in 1373', Margraviate of Brandenburg page) yet this shape keeps it to 1384; it is removed here and belongs to margraviate-of-brandenburg and Charles IV's lands. Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut were a separate county (county-of-holland dossier, 1363-1432), not Bavarian land.

correction.text: Bavaria proper; the Dutch counties removed

keyframe_review.note: 47.7 k km2 = Bavaria proper 36.2 k + Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut 11.5 k. Bavaria-Straubing held the Dutch lands: 'Scattered lands of Bavaria-Straubing, 1353-1432', 'between 1353 and 1432' governed by dukes of Bavaria-Straubing, whose lands the page names as Straubing, Holland and Hainaut. Those counties are the county-of-holland state; the Duchy of Bavaria page says 'the Dutch counties fell to Burgundy in 1436'. They are removed from the Bavarian outline.

correction.text: Bavaria proper; Luxembourg and the Dutch counties removed

keyframe_review.note: 58.0 k km2 = the 47.7 k km2 of 1385-1421 plus 10.3 k km2, the size of Cliopatria's Duchy of Luxembourg (10.26 k km2, which has its own row from 1429). The Duchy of Luxembourg page lists '1415-1419: Elizabeth of Görlitz' and, for 1419-1425, a 'John the Fearless' under that name; nothing opened ties Luxembourg to the Bavarian dukes. Luxembourg and Holland are removed pending the duchy-of-luxembourg and county-of-holland dossiers. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Bavaria proper after the Straubing division; Dutch counties removed

keyframe_review.note: 47.8 k km2 = Bavaria proper plus the Dutch counties. The division of the Straubing lands: 'in 1429 under arbitration of the emperor' (Straubing page); 'In 1429 parts of Bavaria-Straubing were united with Bavaria-Landshut' (Landshut page). The Straubing lands in Lower Bavaria are inside the 1450 outline; the Dutch counties are not Bavarian land.

correction.text: Bavaria proper; the Dutch counties are Burgundian

keyframe_review.note: 46.9 k km2 still contains the Dutch counties. 'the Dutch counties fell to Burgundy in 1436' (Duchy of Bavaria page); the County of Hainaut page: 'Already in 1428, effective control of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland was acquired by Philip the Good' and 'In 1432 Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip'; the County of Holland page: 'From 1433 onward it was part of the Burgundian Netherlands'. Cliopatria hands them to Burgundy only in 1450. Removed from the Bavarian outline.

correction.text: Bavaria proper

keyframe_review.note: 47.7 k km2: Bavaria proper plus the Dutch counties, which were Burgundian from 1433 (County of Holland page) or 1436 (Duchy of Bavaria page). Removed from the Bavarian outline; the Burgundy dossier (eu-10) and county-of-holland carry them.

36.2 k km2: Upper and Lower Bavaria after the Bavaria-Straubing division (1429) and the annexation of Bavaria-Ingolstadt by Landshut ('Annexed Bavaria-Ingolstadt: 1447', Landshut page). The duchy is still split between the Munich and Landshut lines until 1503, which are one state here. No infobox area on the pages.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1459-1504 only

keyframe_review.note: 36.2 k km2 holds until the Landshut War. The shape stays correct for 1459-1504; the 1505 arbitration changed the land (duchy-of-bavaria_1505), while Cliopatria changes the outline only in 1507.

correction.text: Bavaria after the Landshut settlement

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1505-1506: the arbitration of 30 July 1505 at the Diet of Cologne left the Munich line 'the rest of the territory', while 'Otto Henry and Philip retained Palatinate-Neuburg (Junge Pfalz)' and 'Maximilian took Kufstein, receiving the surrender of Rattenberg, Schwaz, Zillertal, Brixental, Traunstein, Kitzbühel and Reichenhall'. The smaller outline (34.8 k km2) is Cliopatria's from 1507; the Duchy of Bavaria page puts the Tyrolean offices' loss in 1504. Two years earlier than Cliopatria.

34.8 k km2 for 1507-1618: the reunited duchy. 'In spite of the decree of 1506, Albert's oldest son William IV was compelled to grant a share in the government in 1516, an arrangement which lasted until the death of Louis in 1545': a joint reign, no division of land. Munich is capital 'from 1505'. In December 1607 Maximilian's troops occupied Donauwörth, which the outline does not show (see notes). No infobox area on the page.
34.7 k km2. 'he made a treaty with Ferdinand II, Holy Roman Emperor in October 1619' (Maximilian I page); the Catholic League dates from 1609. No land change before 1622 is dated by the page.

46.4 k km2: Bavaria plus the Upper Palatinate (+11.7 k km2). 'the electoral dignity and territory of the Upper Palatinate was conferred upon his loyal cousin' (Electorate page, no year); the infobox gives 'Granted electoral dignity: 1623' and the Maximilian I page 'Reign: 25 February 1623'. Cliopatria starts the larger outline in 1622, a year before the page's 1623; the page is silent on any occupation in 1621-1622. Kept as drawn.

46.4 k km2, unchanged. 'Subsequently Ferdinand II released Upper Austria as a pawn for Maximilian until 1628' (Maximilian I page): a pledge whose start the page does not date and which the outline does not show (see notes).

26.0 k km2, 20.4 k km2 smaller than the 46.4 k km2 before. 'Early in 1632 Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden marched into the electorate and occupied Munich'; the Electorate page: 'In 1632 the Swedes invaded'. Neither page says what the Swedes held or when they left, so the outline cannot be checked: unverified, page budget. The ledger draws the Swedish occupation as a hatched zone around Munich.

46.4 k km2 again. Peace of Westphalia: 'By this treaty it was agreed that Maximilian would retain the electoral dignity, which was made hereditary in his family along with the Upper Palatinate'; he 'had to give up the Lower Palatinate, which was restored to Charles Louis'. No border change is dated between 1648 and 1701.

47.8 k km2: 1.3 k km2 more than the usual 46.4 k, west to 9.8 E. The Electorate page says Maximilian II Emanuel fought 'on the side of France, in the great struggle of the Spanish succession' but does not name any land taken in 1702: unverified, page budget. A confidence-1 bridging gain and loss in the ledger carry the strip.

46.4 k km2 again. Defeat at Blenheim 'on 13 August 1704', 'Placed under the imperial ban, his dominions were temporarily partitioned between Austria and the elector palatine by the Treaty of Ilbersheim', 'crushed by the Austrian occupiers in 1706', 'only restored to him ... at the Treaty of Baden in 1714'. Cliopatria keeps the whole outline as Bavarian; the ledger draws the Austrian occupation 1704-1714 as hatching, owner unchanged.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1741-1742 only

keyframe_review.note: 53.7 k km2 (+7.3 k km2, east to 14.8 E, with 'Czechia' among its modern countries): 'Charles invaded Upper Austria in 1741' and 'capturing Prague in November 1741'; the added cells lie between 48.0 and 49.9 N (Upper Austria and southern Bohemia on the map) and do not reach Prague. 'Charles was crowned king of Bohemia in Prague on 19 December 1741' and 'Most of Bohemia was lost in December 1742'. The outline holds for 1741-1742; Cliopatria keeps it to 1743, a year too long, so 1743 gets its own keyframe.

correction.text: Bavaria proper, as in 1706-1740

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1743: the 1741 conquests were gone after December 1742. 'In 1743, his troops and their allies took Bavaria' and 'Charles was able to return to Munich in April' before 'losing Bavaria again after his French allies were defeated and withdrew to the Rhine'; the page has Bavaria changing hands in 1743, which the ledger approximates as one Austrian occupation from 1742 to October 1744.
46.6 k km2. 'In October 1744, Charles regained Munich and returned, this time for good.' The Treaty of Füssen of 22 April 1745 (Electorate page) 'obtained the restitution of his dominions'.
46.4 k km2 for 1752-1777. 'At his death, without issue, on 30 December 1777, the Bavarian line of the Wittelsbachs became extinct.' Cliopatria has no shape for 1778-1779.

correction.text: Bavaria, the Palatinate, Jülich and Berg under Charles Theodore

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1778-1779, which Cliopatria lacks: the succession of Charles Theodore, Elector Palatine, 'proclaimed' on 3 January 1778; the war ran '3 July 1778 - 13 May 1779'. The union of Bavaria with the Palatinate, Jülich and Berg is drawn as in Cliopatria's 1780 outline; Lower Bavaria is a contested zone (ledger).

55.6 k km2: the union after 1777, 'the Electoral Palatinate, to which the duchies of Jülich and Berg had been added, was thus reunited with Bavaria' (infobox: 'Personal union with Electorate of the Palatinate: 1777'). The Innviertel (about 2.2 k km2) went to Austria at Teschen on 13 May 1779. The pages give no infobox area; the outline is kept as drawn. The Electoral Palatinate has no dossier of its own (see notes).
53.8 k km2, 1.8 k km2 less than 1780-1790; no page opened dates or explains it: unverified, page budget.

correction.text: the 1793 outline kept: the left-bank lands stay Bavarian under French occupation until 1801

keyframe_review.note: 44.9 k km2 drops 9.0 k km2 on the left bank. 'In 1792 the French Revolutionary Army overran the Palatinate' and 'By the Treaty of Lunéville (9 February 1801) Bavaria lost the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich.' Until the treaty the land was Bavarian but occupied, so the owner's outline keeps it (hatched via the occupation events) and the loss is drawn in 1801.

correction.text: the 1793 outline kept while the left bank is occupied

keyframe_review.note: 44.8 k km2 for the single year 1796. 'granted an armistice in return for a heavy contribution (7 September 1796)' after Moreau's invasion of Bavaria itself. Same correction as 1794: the left bank stays in the owner's outline while occupied.

correction.text: the 1793 outline kept for 1797-1800 only

keyframe_review.note: 44.9 k km2 for 1797-1802. Lunéville was signed on 9 February 1801, so the left bank belongs to Bavaria in the owner's outline only for 1797-1800; the 1797 outline is right from 1801 (duchy-of-bavaria_1801).

correction.text: Bavaria and the Palatine possessions east of the Rhine, without the lands ceded at Lunéville

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1801-1802: after Lunéville the outline of 44.9 k km2 without the Palatinate, Zweibrücken and Jülich (west of 6.7 E) is the Bavarian state.

correction.text: the 1803 outline plus the Duchy of Berg, still Max Joseph's

keyframe_review.note: 55.6 k km2 for 1803-1804 after the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss: 'The Final Recess of the Imperial Deputation ... of 25 February 1803' gave Bavaria 'Augsburg; Bamberg; Freising; Passau; Würzburg' and imperial cities; the page's table counts Bavaria's losses at 10,000 km2 and gains at 14,000 km2 (net 4,000), against +10.7 k km2 here, 0.76 of the 14,000 km2 gained (the net of 4,000 km2 would be a ratio of 2.7, because the 10,000 km2 lost are the left bank, which this series takes out in 1801). Cliopatria's outline begins at 9.5 E in 1803: it drops Berg, although 'On 15 March 1806 Max Joseph had ceded the Duchy of Berg to Napoleon' (Electorate page). Berg is added back as a radius around Düsseldorf, 'which became the capital of Berg' (Battle of Worringen page).

correction.text: the 1805 outline plus the Duchy of Berg

keyframe_review.note: 47.0 k km2 for 1805, 8.6 k km2 below 1803-1804, which no page explains ('Würzburg, obtained in 1803, was to be ceded by Bavaria to the elector of Salzburg in exchange for Tyrol' is future in the Electorate page): unverified, page budget. Berg is added back as above. Tyrol and Vorarlberg come on 26 December 1805 ('while Bavaria received Tyrol and Vorarlberg') and are in the ledger, not in this outline.

ledger.note: 1260: the Duchy of Bavaria enters the map as Louis II's Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate, after the partition of 1255. 'When the Wittelsbach country was divided in 1255 among Otto's sons, Louis received the Palatinate and Upper Bavaria, while his brother duke Henry XIII of Bavaria received Lower Bavaria.' 1260 is where Cliopatria's row begins; the page's date for the land is 1255.

1268: Louis II inherits part of the Hohenstaufen lands. 'After the young prince's execution in Naples in 1268, Louis inherited some of Conradin's possessions in Swabia.' The region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1272 and 1260 outlines (my reading); the page names Swabia only.

region.text: 'the Rhine Palatinate, and a later so-called Upper Palatinate'

ledger.note: 1329: the Treaty of Pavia gives the Palatinates away. 'In the 1329 Treaty of Pavia, Emperor Louis divided ownership in a Palatine region, with the Rhine Palatinate, and a later so-called Upper Palatinate.' The Louis IV page: 'In the treaty, he gave the Palatinate to the two dukes, and inherited both Upper and Lower Bavaria for himself.' The region is Cliopatria's 1305 outline minus the 1450 outline.

1340: Louis IV reunites Bavaria. 'With the death of duke John I in 1340 Louis inherited Lower Bavaria and then reunited the duchy of Bavaria.' Lower Bavaria is Cliopatria's House of Wittelsbach outline (row ends 1332).

1342: Tyrol passes to the Wittelsbach. 'In 1342 Louis also acquired Tyrol for the Wittelsbach' (the County of Tyrol page: 'In 1342 she married Louis V of Wittelsbach, then Margrave of Brandenburg'). A personal union through the marriage of Louis V and Margaret.

1349: the Wittelsbach possessions are divided again, 'after Günther's early death in 1349 and divided the Wittelsbach possessions among themselves again' (the sentence's subject is cut off in the extract read; it follows the account of Louis IV's sons). A division among the dynasty's lines; the state and its colour continue.

1353: Bavaria-Landshut is created. 'Four years later the inheritance was divided again in the Treaty of Regensburg 1353; Stephen received the new Duchy of Bavaria-Landshut' (infobox 'Established: 3 June 1353'); Bavaria-Straubing is governed by its own dukes 'between 1353 and 1432' (Straubing page). Lines of one state, one colour.

1363: Tyrol goes to the Habsburgs. 'she bequeathed the county to Rudolph IV of Habsburg, Duke of Austria in 1363'. The Duchy of Bavaria page has 'In 1369, Tyrol fell through the Treaty of Schärding to the Habsburgs' and the Tyrol page 'He was recognized by the House of Wittelsbach in 1369'.

1392: 'in 1392 Bavaria-Landshut was divided for the three dukes and so Bavaria-Munich and Bavaria-Ingolstadt were split off' (Landshut page); 'Four Duchies existed after the division of 1392' (Duchy of Bavaria page). 'These dukes often waged war against each other.' Lines of one state.

1429: the Straubing inheritance is divided 'under arbitration of the emperor' among Bavaria-Munich, Bavaria-Landshut and Bavaria-Ingolstadt (Straubing page); 'In 1429 parts of Bavaria-Straubing were united with Bavaria-Landshut' (Landshut page).
1447: Bavaria-Landshut annexes Bavaria-Ingolstadt (infobox 'Annexed Bavaria-Ingolstadt: 1447').

1503: the Landshut inheritance is fought over. 'After George's death on 1 December 1503, this unresolved dispute escalated into the War of the Succession of Landshut.' The page does not date the first campaign; the death of the last Landshut duke is the date used.
1505: arbitration ends the war. 'The war ended in 1505 with a decision through arbitration by Emperor Maximilian I on 30 July 1505 at the Diet of Cologne.'

1505: Bavaria is reunited under the Munich line. 'The rest of the territory went to the Munich line of the House of Wittelsbach.' The Duchy of Bavaria page: 'Duke Albrecht IV of Bavaria-Munich united Bavaria in 1503 through war and primogeniture' (infobox 'Reunification: 1503'), and Munich is capital 'from 1505'.

1505: Palatinate-Neuburg is carved out. 'Otto Henry and Philip retained Palatinate-Neuburg (Junge Pfalz), a fragmented region from the upper Danube.' The region is my reading: a radius around Neuburg an der Donau, 'chosen as the capital of the new state'.

region.text: 'the territory around Kufstein' with Rattenberg and Kitzbühel

ledger.note: 1505: Maximilian I takes the Tyrolean offices. 'Maximilian took Kufstein, receiving the surrender of Rattenberg, Schwaz, Zillertal, Brixental, Traunstein, Kitzbühel and Reichenhall'; the Duchy of Bavaria page: 'Kufstein, Kitzbühel and Rattenberg in Tirol were lost in 1504'.

region.text: the territory of the Upper Palatinate

ledger.note: 1623: Maximilian receives the Upper Palatinate. 'the electoral dignity and territory of the Upper Palatinate was conferred upon his loyal cousin' (page gives no year; the infobox 'Granted electoral dignity: 1623'); 'Maximilian retained these gains at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.' Cliopatria's outline grows in 1622.

1623: the Duchy becomes an Electorate. 'his title was elevated to that of prince-elector of the Holy Roman Empire at the 1623 Diet of Regensburg' (Maximilian reigns as Elector from 25 February 1623). Same state, same colour.
1632: the Swedes occupy Munich. 'Early in 1632 Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden marched into the electorate and occupied Munich.'

1635: the Swedish occupation ends. Page silent: the Maximilian I page does not say when the Swedes left; the year is inferred from Cliopatria's reduced 1632-1635 shape, which returns to full size in 1636.

region.text: the strip west of the Lech that Cliopatria adds in 1702

ledger.note: 1702: a western strip joins Bavaria in Cliopatria's outline. Page silent: the Electorate page names no land taken in 1702; the region is Cliopatria's 1702 outline minus its 1701 one.

1704: Austria occupies Bavaria after Blenheim. 'He shared in the defeat at the Battle of Blenheim, near Höchstädt, on 13 August 1704. Placed under the imperial ban, his dominions were temporarily partitioned between Austria and the elector palatine by the Treaty of Ilbersheim.' The page dates the ban to 1706 and the Ilbersheim year is not on it, so 1704 is a bridge; the elector palatine's share is not drawn separately.

region.text: the strip west of the Lech that Cliopatria adds in 1702

ledger.note: 1706: the western strip leaves the outline. Page silent; the region is Cliopatria's 1702 outline minus its 1701 one, which Cliopatria drops in 1706.
1714: Bavaria is restored. 'only restored to him, harried and exhausted, at the Treaty of Baden in 1714' (infobox 'Imperial ban reversed: 1714').

region.text: the lands overrun in Upper Austria and Bohemia in 1741

ledger.note: 1741: Charles Albert overruns Upper Austria and Bohemia. 'Charles invaded Upper Austria in 1741 and planned to conquer Vienna'; 'capturing Prague in November 1741' (French troops under Belle-Isle); 'Charles was crowned king of Bohemia in Prague on 19 December 1741'. The region is Cliopatria's 1741 outline minus its 1740 one (about 8 k km2 between 10.3 and 14.7 E), which does not reach Prague itself.

region.text: Bavaria occupied by Maria Theresa's troops

ledger.note: 1742: Austria overruns Bavaria. 'Shortly after his coronation, most of Charles's territories were overrun by the Austrians, and Bavaria was occupied by the troops of Maria Theresa.' The coronation was 12 February 1742; the page gives no year for the occupation itself.

region.text: most of Bohemia and the lands overrun in 1741

ledger.note: 1742: Bohemia is lost. 'Most of Bohemia was lost in December 1742, when the Austrians allowed the French ... an honourable capitulation.' The page does not date the loss of Upper Austria; the whole 1741 gain is closed here and in the 1743 keyframe.

region.text: Bavaria occupied by Maria Theresa's troops

ledger.note: 1744: Charles VII is back in Munich. 'In October 1744, Charles regained Munich and returned, this time for good.' The Treaty of Füssen of 22 April 1745 ends the war: Austria 'recognised the legitimacy of Charles's election' and the Electorate page says the treaty of 22 April 1745 'obtained the restitution of his dominions'.

region.text: the Electoral Palatinate with the duchies of Jülich and Berg

ledger.note: 1777: the Bavarian Wittelsbach line dies out and the Palatinate, Jülich and Berg join Bavaria. 'At his death, without issue, on 30 December 1777, the Bavarian line of the Wittelsbachs became extinct ... the Electoral Palatinate, to which the duchies of Jülich and Berg had been added, was thus reunited with Bavaria.' The region is Cliopatria's 1780 outline minus its 1752 one.

region.text: Lower Bavaria, ceded to Austria by the secret agreement of 3 January 1778

ledger.note: 1778: Lower Bavaria is claimed by Austria. 'Charles Theodore ceded Lower Bavaria to Austria in exchange for uncontested succession to the remainder of the electorate (3 January 1778)'; the war itself began 3 July 1778. The page mentions Austrian troops at Mindelheim and an 'Austrian administration at Straubing' without dates. The Austrian claim rested on 'a dubious and ancient grant'.
1779: Teschen ends the dispute. Treaty of Teschen 'signed on 13 May 1779': 'Maria Theresa returned Lower Bavaria to Charles Theodore'.

1779: the Innviertel goes to Austria. 'By the peace of Teschen (13 May 1779) the Innviertel was ceded to Austria' (Electorate page); Austria 'kept the so-called Innviertel', 'a 2,200-square-kilometer strip of land in the drainage basin of the Inn river'.

region.text: the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich

ledger.note: 1792: France overruns the Palatinate. 'In 1792 the French Revolutionary Army overran the Palatinate.' The region is Cliopatria's 1793 outline minus its 1794 one (the Palatinate, Zweibrücken and Jülich).

region.text: the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich

ledger.note: 1801: the occupation ends in cession. 'By the Treaty of Lunéville (9 February 1801) Bavaria lost the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich.' The ceding party is the French Consulate of 1801; the counterpart string is kept equal to the occupation's start.

region.text: the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich

ledger.note: 1801: Lunéville. 'By the Treaty of Lunéville (9 February 1801) Bavaria lost the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich.'

1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg. The Final Recess of 25 February 1803 lists 'Augsburg; Bamberg; Freising; Passau; Würzburg;' under the Elector of Bavaria, and the Electorate page: 'Bavaria received the bishoprics of Würzburg, Bamberg, Augsburg and Freisingen, part of that of Passau'. Bavarian troops had entered Bamberg and Würzburg in August 1802. The region is a radius around the bishop's city.

Bavarian troops had entered Bamberg and Würzburg in August 1802. The region is a radius around the bishop's city.

The Final Recess of 25 February 1803 lists 'Augsburg; Bamberg; Freising; Passau; Würzburg;' under the Elector of Bavaria, and the Electorate page: 'Bavaria received the bishoprics of Würzburg, Bamberg, Augsburg and Freisingen, part of that of Passau'. Bavarian troops had entered Bamberg and Würzburg in August 1802. The region is a radius around the bishop's city.

The Final Recess of 25 February 1803 lists 'Augsburg; Bamberg; Freising; Passau; Würzburg;' under the Elector of Bavaria, and the Electorate page: 'Bavaria received the bishoprics of Würzburg, Bamberg, Augsburg and Freisingen, part of that of Passau'. Bavarian troops had entered Bamberg and Würzburg in August 1802. The region is a radius around the bishop's city.

1805: Tyrol and Vorarlberg come to Bavaria. The Peace of Pressburg 'was signed in Pressburg (today Bratislava) on 26 December 1805' ... 'while Bavaria received Tyrol and Vorarlberg'. Eichstätt and Burgau are named in the Electorate page's truncated sentence and are not claimed here.

region.text: the Free Imperial City of Augsburg

ledger.note: 1805: Augsburg. 'Augsburg, previously an independent Free Imperial City, was ceded to Bavaria.' The German mediatisation page says 'Augsburg was annexed by Bavaria shortly thereafter in 1805' in its text and 1806 in its table, so the year is uncertain.

region.text: the electorate's last outline, with Tyrol, Vorarlberg and Berg

ledger.note: 1805: the last year of the electorate. 'Duke and Elector Maximilian IV Joseph was proclaimed King Maximilian I Joseph on 1 January 1806'; the Pressburg treaty of 26 December 1805 recognised 'the kingly titles assumed by the Electors of Bavaria and Württemberg'. The land passes to the Kingdom of Bavaria, which also holds Berg only until 15 March 1806.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Landshut
wars.outcome: Arbitration by Emperor Maximilian I on 30 July 1505 at the Diet of Cologne: the Munich line kept the rest, the Palatine heirs got Palatinate-Neuburg, Maximilian took Kufstein, Rattenberg, Kitzbühel and other places, and Nuremberg gained Lauf, Hersbruck and Altdorf.
wars.note: Nuremberg's gains lie outside Cliopatria's Bavarian outline and are not a Bavarian event here.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War

zones.text: Munich and the electorate, occupied by the Swedes in 1632

wars.outcome: Maximilian kept the electoral dignity and the Upper Palatinate at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 and gave up the Lower Palatinate; the Swedes occupied Munich in 1632, and the French and Swedes ravaged the land after the Truce of Ulm of 1647 was broken.
wars.note: Bavaria's part only. The first fighting dated on the pages opened is 8 November 1620 (White Mountain); the pages do not give the war's own start year.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession

zones.text: the electorate, partitioned between Austria and the elector palatine

wars.outcome: Defeat at Blenheim on 13 August 1704, the imperial ban (1706) and Austrian occupation, and restoration at the Treaty of Baden in 1714.
wars.note: Bavaria's part only. The first dated event on the pages opened is Blenheim; the page does not give the war's start year.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: Charles Albert took Prague (November 1741), was crowned king of Bohemia (19 December 1741) and emperor (12 February 1742); Bohemia was lost in December 1742 and Bavaria occupied; he regained Munich in October 1744; the Treaty of Füssen of 22 April 1745 restored his dominions.

wars.name: War of the Bavarian Succession
wars.outcome: Treaty of Teschen, 13 May 1779: Austria kept the Innviertel and returned Lower Bavaria to Charles Theodore.
wars.note: The page's infobox lists the Habsburg monarchy against Prussia, Saxony and Bavaria.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars

zones.text: the Palatinate and the duchies of Zweibrücken and Jülich

wars.outcome: France overran the Palatinate in 1792, invaded Bavaria in 1795-1796 (armistice of 7 September 1796), and at Lunéville on 9 February 1801 Bavaria lost the Palatinate, Zweibrücken and Jülich.
wars.note: Bavaria's part only; Moreau's invasion of Bavaria itself is dated 1795 on the page and the armistice 7 September 1796.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805: Bavaria received Tyrol and Vorarlberg and Austria recognised the royal titles of Bavaria and Württemberg.
wars.note: Bavaria's part only. The Pressburg page names only 'the Third Coalition'; Bavaria was France's ally.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened for these years: partitions among the dynasty's lines, scattered possessions (Tyrol, the Dutch counties) and outlines drawn by Cliopatria; the Palatinates in 1329, the Landshut settlement of 1505 and Westphalia in 1648 move the land but give no lines.

Treaty lines: Teschen (13 May 1779) fixes the Innviertel frontier, Lunéville (9 February 1801) the left-bank cession, the Final Recess (25 February 1803) the bishoprics, Pressburg (26 December 1805) Tyrol and Vorarlberg. The Palatine, Jülich and Berg outliers between 1777 and 1802 stay approximate.

notes:
BAVARIA. What this dossier does. Cliopatria's 'Duchy of Bavaria' row is a lump of Wittelsbach lands: from the opened pages and the areas, 1352-1362 (97.2 k km2) is Bavaria proper (36.2 k, the 1450 outline) + Brandenburg (about 44 k) + Tyrol (about 16.8 k); 1363-1384 (92.1 k) is Bavaria + Brandenburg + the Dutch counties; 1385-1449 (47.7-47.8 k) is Bavaria + Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, and 1422-1428 (58.0 k) adds a Luxembourg-sized 10.3 k. Cliopatria's 'Margraviate of Brandenburg' row does the same in reverse for 1326-1351 (77.8-80.5 k km2): Brandenburg + Bavaria. Rule applied here: land of a state that has its own row or dossier is taken out of the Bavarian outline (Brandenburg, Holland, Luxembourg); land with no dossier yet (Tyrol 1342-1363, the Palatine and Jülich-Berg union 1777-1802) is kept and flagged. All of these dynastic unions are personal unions of the Wittelsbach.

FOR OTHER DOSSIERS. margraviate-of-brandenburg (eu-09, another part) must remove Bavaria from its 1326-1351 shapes and draw Brandenburg itself for 1352-1384 (Wittelsbach margraves to 1373, then Charles IV); county-of-holland (this batch) now runs to 1433 and carries Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut for 1363-1432; duchy-of-luxembourg needs 1415-1428; house-of-wittelsbach (Cliopatria's Lower Bavaria, 1260-1332) is the Lower Bavaria that rejoins this state in 1340, and Lower Bavaria is nobody's in 1333-1339; a County of Tyrol dossier (1342-1363 at least) and an Electoral Palatinate dossier (Rhenish Palatinate and Upper Palatinate 1329-1623, Palatinate-Neuburg from 1505, 1777 union) are needed. The prince-bishoprics of Würzburg, Bamberg, Freising, Augsburg and Passau are counterparts of the 1803 gains.

START. The Duchy of Bavaria is far older than 1260 (the page lists the first partition in 1255 and Regensburg as capital until 1255); the dossier starts where Cliopatria's row starts, with the 1255 partition as the page's date for the land. Pre-1260 Bavaria is not reviewed.

PAGE BUDGET (up to 14): 14 pages were opened for the duchy; the County of Holland, County of Hainaut and Duchy of Luxembourg pages (opened for the sister dossiers) are cited only for the removal of the Dutch counties and Luxembourg. The Louis II, Duke of Upper Bavaria title did not load (url_not_found); Louis_the_Strict was used instead. No page opened gives an infobox area for any year, so no area check against Cliopatria is possible except the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss table (gains of 14,000 km2 against +10.7 k km2 in the 1803 shape, a ratio of 0.76).

UNVERIFIED (page budget or page silent): the 1279 and 1791 outline changes; the 1702-1705 strip (bridged at confidence 1); the 1632-1635 outline of 26.0 k km2; the 1805 outline (8.6 k km2 less than 1803-1804); the Luxembourg strip of 1422-1428. Not entered because the pages give no date or no end: Maximilian's occupation of Donauwörth ('In December 1607 his troops occupied the city'), the Upper Austria pledge ('until 1628'), the Bavarian hold on the Lower Palatinate until 1648 ('had to give up the Lower Palatinate'), Nuremberg's 1505 gains (outside the outline), the Bavarian invasion of Austria in 1741 (Upper Austria) and Berg's cession on 15 March 1806 (after the dossier's last year). Rulers are omitted: no page opened gives a complete list (a list of rulers of Bavaria page is needed). Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: Innviertel (region), Neuburg an der Donau, Kufstein, Freising (places).

CONFLICTS BETWEEN PAGES: the Louis IV page says at Pavia (1329) Louis 'inherited both Upper and Lower Bavaria for himself' and also that Lower Bavaria came to him in 1340; the dated 1340 sentence is used. The Duchy page dates the loss of Kufstein, Kitzbühel and Rattenberg to 1504, the Landshut War page to the 1505 arbitration. The Electorate page says the Swedes 'invaded' in 1632 and the Maximilian page that they occupied Munich 'early in 1632'. The mediatisation page dates Augsburg's annexation to 1805 in its text and 1806 in its table. Family 'germany' follows the colour registry's note that Bavaria is light blue.
